note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

precepts.why:
David asked Achish, “let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there”, and “Achish gave him Ziklag that day: wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day.”

That is the Ziklag of chapter 30. Notice how this connects to the reading in chapter 27. While David and his men were away with Achish, “the Amalekites had invaded the south, and Ziklag, and smitten Ziklag, and burned it with fire”, and taken the women captive. Yet “they slew not any, either great or small, but carried them away.”

note.label: 1 Samuel 30: David Recovers All at Ziklag

precepts.why:
“David and his men went up, and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites: for those nations were of old the inhabitants of the land.” “And David smote the land, and left neither man nor woman alive.” This is the raid the Amalekites answered at Ziklag.

Now the Amalekites came back and smote Ziklag the same way, taking David's wives and the families of his men while they were gone up with Achish. David and his men found the city “burned with fire; and their wives, and their sons, and their daughters, were taken captives”, and they “lifted up their voice and wept, until they had no more power to weep.”

David's two wives were taken, “Ahinoam the Jezreelitess, and Abigail the wife of Nabal the Carmelite.” “David was greatly distressed; for the people spake of stoning him”, every man grieved for his sons and his daughters: “but David encouraged himself in the Lord his God.”

points: David said in his heart, I shall now perish one day by the hand of Saul: there is nothing better for me than that I should speedily escape into the land of the Philistines, and Saul shall despair of me, to seek me any more in any coast of Israel.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: David passed over with the six hundred men that were with him unto Achish the son of Maoch, king of Gath, every man with his household, David with his two wives, Ahinoam the Jezreelitess and Abigail the Carmelitess, Nabal's wife. When it was told Saul that David was fled to Gath, he sought no more again for him.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: David said to Achish, If I have found grace in thine eyes, let them give me a place in some town in the country, that I may dwell there: for why should thy servant dwell in the royal city with thee? So Achish gave him Ziklag that day; wherefore Ziklag pertaineth unto the kings of Judah unto this day.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: The time that David dwelt in the country of the Philistines was a full year and four months.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: David and his men went up and invaded the Geshurites, and the Gezrites, and the Amalekites, for those nations were of old the inhabitants of the land, as thou goest to Shur, even unto the land of Egypt; and David smote the land, left neither man nor woman alive, took away the sheep, the oxen, the asses, the camels, and the apparel, and returned to Achish.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: When Achish asked, Whither have ye made a road to day? David said, Against the south of Judah, and against the south of the Jerahmeelites, and against the south of the Kenites; and he saved neither man nor woman alive to bring tidings to Gath, saying, Lest they should tell on us.

note.label: 1 Samuel 27: David Dwells in the Land of the Philistines

points: Achish believed David, saying, He hath made his people Israel utterly to abhor him; therefore he shall be my servant for ever. So the session closes with David departed out of the presence of Saul, dwelling with Achish in the land of the Philistines at Gath.
